This project will use the data included in the nycflights13 package. 

Suppose you work for United Airlines (carrier code UA). To improve both efficiency and customer satisfaction, you've been asked to study departure delays. 

Prepare a report that utilizes the exploratory data analysis methods that we have been studying, and permutation tests, to analyze departure delays. 

This report should be written for a general audience, not a technical one. This means that you should be clearly explaining everything without assuming that the audience has any specialized knowledge. It also means that you should use clear words and phrases, rather than variable names, when labeling and discussing your plots and other results.

Your report should address the relationship between departure delays and each of the following:

Time of day
Time of year
Temperature
Wind speed
Precipitation
Visibility
For each of these factors, you can decide whether to use the original dep_delay variable, or the late and very_late variables you created for the first homework assignment (for some questions, you may only be able to conduct a permutation test (based on what we've learned so far) if you use the late and very_late variables). If there are circumstances where you feel it is appropriate to create new variables based on the other factors being analyzed, you may do so, but be sure to clearly indicate that you have done that. 

Your report should include the following:

Introduction. This should include an explanation of what you are investigating, what data you've used, and context for your work.
Data Methodology. Describe how the data was prepared, cleaned, merged, etc. 
Results. Include your exploratory data analysis and your permutation tests for each variable of interest, and discuss and interpret these results. 
Discussion. Describe the overall take-aways from your study, and what future follow-up work might be of interest to expand on it. 


# Introduction

## Import Library and Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(nycflights13)
```

```{r}
glimpse(flights)
```
```{r}
glimpse(weather)
```


# Data Cleansing
## Filter
Filter on United Airlines flights only (carrier: "UA")

```{r}
ua_flights <- flights %>%
  filter(carrier == "UA")
glimpse(ua_flights)
```

## Merge
* flights and weather datasets should be merged

```{r}
ua_flights_weather <- ua_flights |>
  left_join(
    weather,
    by = c("origin", "year", "month", "day", "hour")
  )

glimpse(ua_flights_weather)
```
```{r}
ua_flights_weather %>%
  summarise(
    total_flights = n(),
    average_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
    delay_sd = sd(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
```
The standard deviation of 35.72 suggests a large variation in departure delays.


## Handle missing/erroneous values


Take a look at missing values for our key data

```{r}
ua_flights_weather |>
  summarise(
    total_flights = n(),
    missing_dep_delay = sum(is.na(dep_delay)),
    missing_temp = sum(is.na(temp)),
    missing_wind_speed = sum(is.na(wind_speed)),
    missing_precipitation = sum(is.na(precip)),
    missing_visibility = sum(is.na(visib))
  )
```

The merged dataset contains 58,665 United Airlines flight records. An examination of missing values indicates that the dataset is relatively complete. Departure delay has the most missing value with 686 observations missing. Missing values in weather related variables ranges from 304 to 321 observations. Overall, the low percentage of missing values suggests that most observations are available for analysis. However, additional examination is necessary to determine how missing observations should be handled before conducting exploratory analysis and permutation tests.

The above table provides information regarding missing observations per column.
Investigate how many rows are missing data and how many rows are complete. 

```{r}
ua_flights_weather %>%
  summarise(
    total_rows = n(),
    rows_with_missing = sum(
      !complete.cases( # Checks weather each row has missing values. In this case not operation captures rows with missing values.
        dep_delay, temp, wind_speed, precip, visib
      )
    ),
    complete_rows = sum(
      complete.cases(
        dep_delay, temp, wind_speed, precip, visib
      )
    )
  )
```

Out of 58,665 total flight records, 1,003 (1.71%) contain at least one missing value among the five variables examined: departure delay, temperature, wind speed, precipitation, and visibility. The remaining 57,662 records (98.29%) are complete for these variables. Overall, the dataset has a relatively low proportion of missing observations.


## Calculated columns
Create two calculated columns named late and very_late. 
* late <- departure delays greater than 0 minutes
* very_late <- departure delays greater than 30 minutes
```{r}
ua_flights_weather['late'] <- ua_flights_weather$dep_delay > 0
ua_flights_weather['very_late'] <- ua_flights_weather$dep_delay > 30

```
```{r}
glimpse(ua_flights_weather)
```
